extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), local and state emergency responders, PIO trainees and spokespersons
extracted.subtask_short: PIO training: news releases and JIC
extracted.subtask_description: Training and resource descriptions for public information officers on writing news releases, conducting media relations, operating within the Joint Information System/Center (JIS/JIC), and performing PIO duties during emergencies. Emphasizes practical skills, protocols, and use of established guidance (NIMS, CERC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply PIO skills to major emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of public information skills to a major emergency or disaster situation (APIO course intent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplished through lectures and exercises over four days; prerequisite: basic state-level PIO course (waiver possible for experienced PIOs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of NIMS public information systems and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define NIMS public information systems to include onsite operations, the Joint Information System (JIS), and the Joint Information Center (JIC), and how they relate to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course objective for IS-702; also recommends completion of IS-700 for background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand JIS/JIC processes for information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the JIS/JIC process of gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating information by public information and incident management personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes factors to consider during preparedness, response and recovery stages; listed in NIMS guidance document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify agencies, roles, and integration within JIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify each agency involved in given emergency situations and the role of each in the JIS to ensure appropriate situational awareness information is communicated to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers integration with federal PIOs and support, ESF #15 field-level organization, and pre-identified tools for cross-jurisdictional communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify resource requirements for public information systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify typical resource requirements for public information systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IS-702 objective — includes staffing, facilities, communications tools, and other logistical needs at various incident stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Joint Information Center (JIC) function and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the function of the Joint Information Center within the Incident Command System (ICS), its organizational structure, and roles/responsibilities of JIC staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course O1333 objective — provides examples of JIC organizations and functions at escalating incident stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering/verifying/coordination considerations during incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider factors when gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating information to the public and additional stakeholders during an incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIMS basic guidance outlines checklists and considerations to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and appropriate coordination across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dissemination tools (websites, blogs, other media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tools to help disseminate emergency and preparedness information to the public, such as web sites and web blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIMS guidance emphasizes selecting appropriate channels and maintaining consistent, coordinated messages across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate messages accurately, quickly, consistently, and empathetically
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate messages to the public accurately, quickly, consistently, and empathetically; the right message at the right time by the right person could save lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FF4054 (Advanced PIO) emphasizes Crisis Emergency Risk Communication (CERC) principles and pandemic-specific messaging resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CERC (CDC) and pandemic communication resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss and use Crisis Emergency Risk Communication (CERC) resources developed by CDC, including pandemic-specific guidance such as 'By Leaders for Leaders' and 'Pandemic Influenza.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FF4054 course objective — recommended for LPHA and hospital representatives preparing for pandemic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral and written communications competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate oral and written communications skills necessary for PIO duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FF1052/FF1052-style courses focus on practical exercises to build clear writing and effective speaking for interacting with media and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and work effectively with the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how the media operates and how to work cooperatively with journalists and newsroom personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers 'who's who' in the newsroom, building relationships, and recognizing the media's needs and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and nurture relationships with area media representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate understanding of the need for PIOs to establish and nurture good working relationships with local media representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dealing with the Media (rural first responders) objective — emphasizes proactive relationship-building before incidents occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how media decides newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate an understanding of how the media decides what is newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps PIOs tailor releases and pitches; included in Dealing with the Media and Preparing News Releases courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the five W's (plus one) and inverted pyramid in newswriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and use the five W's (who, what, when, where, why) plus One in writing news releases and apply the inverted pyramid style in newswriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 Preparing News Releases objective — anchors lead writing and information prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on newsworthy elements with clear, simple language and consistent style
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on newsworthy elements of the story by using clear and simple language and consistency in style and usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 stresses readability and consistency as essential properties of an effective news release; adherence to organizational style is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write lead, body, and headline for a news release
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the lead, body and headline for a news release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical skill taught in 03137 — includes crafting a strong lead that contains top-priority information and headline that summarizes the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of quotations in news releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the importance of quotations in a news release and use them in an appropriate manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 notes quotations add authority and human perspective; they should be accurate, attributable, and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand deadlines and newsroom timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the importance of deadlines in different types of news release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 emphasizes matching release timing to media deadlines (print/broadcast/online) and planning dissemination accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the review and dissemination process for releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the review process for a news release and explain the dissemination process for a news release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 covers internal clearance, approvals, and choosing distribution channels (email, wire services, web postings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for follow-up media questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequately prepare for follow-up questions from the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 and other courses recommend anticipating difficult questions, preparing spokespeople, and developing talking points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and analyze news reports; use Rapid Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectively monitor and analyze news reports, utilizing Rapid Response when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 suggests active media monitoring to correct inaccuracies and respond quickly to developing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop talking points using the 'message triangle'
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop talking points using the 'message triangle' technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 and other courses recommend the message triangle for concise, consistent messaging: main message, supporting points, call to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate and produce news advisories, news releases, PSAs, briefings, and conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the difference between a news release and a news advisory; write an effective news advisory; write effective public service announcements; distinguish between a news release, a news conference and a news briefing; prepare for and conduct a news conference or briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 covers formats, use-cases, content differences, and logistical considerations for each product and event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify criteria and qualities of effective broadcast stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the criteria used to select broadcast media stories and describe four essential qualities contained in effective broadcast news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 emphasizes brevity, clarity, visuals/sound bites, and immediacy for broadcast suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate media interview techniques at emergency scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate techniques for conducting media interviews at the scene of emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dealing with the Media course covers positioning, soundbites, controlling the message, and safety considerations at the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance media needs with first responder operational needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how to balance the needs of the media with those of first responders at the scene of an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course guidance includes protecting operations and safety while providing timely information to media; may involve staging areas and media control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and set staging areas at incident scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how to choose a staging area at the scene of an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dealing with the Media course recommends choosing safe, accessible locations that facilitate interviews while maintaining scene integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize and organize information for clear, accurate public understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize and organize information in a manner that creates clear and accurate understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03137 stresses organization that supports transparency and reduces public confusion during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand organizational benefits and obligations in working with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that news coverage communicates accomplishments and builds public support, and that public institutions have an obligation to share information with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University Guide frames media engagement as mutually beneficial and an institutional responsibility in good and bad times.
